answer: Mass identity fraud is unattractive here not because it is always caught, but because it is never profitable to attempt at scale — the expected loss from slashing and rejection exceeds the expected gain. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.
